posts.title: October 2026 Update
posts.description: October is almost over, and it’s time for another harvest update from Happy Acres. The harvests are surely winding down here, and that is pretty much right on schedule for our garden. The tomatoes are done for, but I am still getting peppers and a few eggplants. It has been a great year for the summer veggies, and we have been well supplied for fresh use and for preserving. I also have a good supply of the Centercut neck pumpkins for our fall and winter use. early October harvest The harvest of hot peppers has slowed a bit but I’m getting plenty of them in now. I’ve made enough hot sauce to last me for a year or so, and I’ve pickled quite a few of them. assortment of hot peppers The sweet peppers have also done great this year, and we have enjoyed them for fresh eating. posts.title: September 2026 Update
posts.description: It’s hard for me to believe, but September is almost over, and it’s time for another harvest update from Happy Acres. Our harvests are slowing down now, and I’m not really unhappy about that! I have been busy now for months hauling in produce and preserving it for later use. It has been a good season here for vegetables, and I have harvested just over 400 pounds so far. Compared to last year’s total of 293 pounds, that is indeed a good amount. I still have to dig the sweet potatoes sometime before frost, which should add to the totals as well. early September harvest The winter squashes have done quite well this year, and we have been enjoying them often with our meals. One variety I’m growing for the first time is a dumpling squash called Honey Bun. The fruits have been averaging just under one pound each for me, and the flesh is sweet and tasty. Like delicata squashes, the skin is tender and edible. I have been cutting these into slices and roasting them like I do the delicata squash

posts.title: It’s Tomato Season!
posts.description: The tomatoes have been rolling in here lately, and I thought I would share pics and details of what I have been harvesting. I have been busy turning them into sauce, and my wife and I made a batch of ketchup a couple of weeks ago. We have also been eating them fresh at every occasion. I’ve harvested a little over 100 pounds so far, and it is looking to be a pretty good year for them, at least in yield. early August tomatoes homemade ketchup jars The taste of the tomatoes this year is quite variable though. Last year, Harvest Moon was outstanding in taste tests. This year is it pretty bland tasting. It’s lovely, but that’s about all it’s got going for it. Harvest Moon tomato Black Angel has been quite variable too, with some tastier than others. It has yielded well though, which is a plus. The jury is still out on whether it will be back next year or not. Black Angel tomato Garden Treasure remains a favorite of both my wife and I, and it has not disappointed us this year.
